The trending Python landscape this week is heavily dominated by agentic tooling, developer productivity utilities, and specialized AI infrastructure. Key repositories include 'microsoft/markitdown', which simplifies data ingestion for LLMs by converting various file formats to Markdown, and 'anthropics/claude-code', an agentic terminal tool that streamlines coding workflows. These tools represent a shift toward making AI agents more capable of interacting with real-world file systems and development environments.

Governance and safety are also emerging as critical themes. 'microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit' provides essential frameworks for policy enforcement and security in autonomous agent systems, addressing the growing need for reliability in production AI. Similarly, 'mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills' offers a standardized library of cybersecurity skills for agents, mapping to industry-standard frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK, which is vital for building secure, enterprise-grade AI.

Efficiency and optimization remain high priorities, as evidenced by 'chopratejas/headroom'. This tool focuses on reducing token consumption for LLMs by compressing logs and RAG chunks, directly addressing the cost and latency bottlenecks in current AI application development. These repositories collectively highlight a maturing ecosystem focused on moving AI from experimental prototypes to robust, governed, and efficient production tools.

prompt_sent:
You are the GitHub Research skill. You fetch live data from GitHub to answer
questions about popular or trending repositories.

Your tool surface is ONE MCP tool: `fetch_url(url)`. Use it. Do not narrate;
do not invent other tools.

Procedure:
  1. Read the QUESTION. Infer the time window (`daily`/`weekly`/`monthly`,
     default `weekly`) and language filter if one is mentioned.
  2. Fetch the trending page:
     `https://github.com/trending/<language>?since=<window>`
     (omit `/<language>` if none was mentioned).
  3. Extract the top 5–10 repos: name (owner/repo), description, stars, URL.

Time budget: keep tool calls to 3 max. Do not retry a thin fetch beyond the
one fallback above.

Output schema (JSON, no prose, no markdown fences):

  {
    "question": "<the question this run answered>",
    "sources": [{"url": "<url>", "title": "<title>"}, ...],
    "findings": "<2–6 short paragraphs of normalised text>"
  }

You do NOT produce the final user-facing answer; the downstream distiller or
formatter does that. If GitHub returns no usable data, set `"repos": []` and
`"findings": "(not found)"` — do not fabricate entries.
